svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Quick brings AI-ready capabilities to existing datasets. AWS Quick makes legacy datasets AI ready through the new technology stack used by its improved visual data preparation experience, a stack for structured data introduced in October 2025 that supports visual multi-step transformations such as Append, Aggregate and Pivot, faster ingestion for larger datasets, and up to 20 times higher cross-source join limits than the legacy experience. The stack powers Dataset Semantics, topics and semantic models, and Dataset Evaluation. When authors edit a supported legacy dataset, Quick automatically opens it in the visual data preparation experience, carrying over its existing data sources, joins, transformations and calculated fields, so authors can add semantics and evaluate answer accuracy without recreating the dataset. Support has been expanded for Google Sheets and Salesforce connectors, JODA date formats, incremental refresh, and preservation of existing unmaterialized calculated columns during legacy dataset upgrades. The substance of enrichment is three text channels with different visibility and different limits. The Dataset Description is a business-level summary visible to all dataset consumers in the UI, with a maximum length of 5,000 characters. Custom Instructions are free-form text instructions specifically consumed by AI agents that guide the AI on how to interpret, query and reason about the dataset, also capped at 5,000 characters. A File Upload accepts a single file in YAML, JSON or TXT format containing catalog-grade semantic metadata exported from third-party tools such as Databricks, dbt or Alation, capped at 50,000 characters, and the documentation states that while this information is used by AI models rather than displayed in the UI it enables catalog-grade metadata at scale. That is the asymmetry worth planning for: the largest instruction channel is the one no human sees in the interface, ten times the size of the two visible fields. Column-level enrichment adds folders, a Column Description capped at 500 characters, and Additional Notes capped at 2,000 characters. There is an explicit warning not to add sensitive information to the Dataset Description or Custom Instructions fields because this information is visible to all dataset viewers. Governance is partly reassuring: all responses respect Row-Level Security and Column-Level Security rules, and authors and author pros with Enterprise licenses can enrich any dataset they own or manage. But access widens automatically: starting June 1 2026, Dataset View permissions are available for Professional subscribers, who gain access automatically if they are a member of a group where a dataset has been shared or a member of a folder containing shared datasets, with no action required from authors or admins, though they cannot create analyses, edit datasets or modify schema. Without enrichment the AI agent only has column names and data types to work with, which are often ambiguous. The capability is available in all supported AWS Quick Regions.
svg.title: The largest instruction channel is the one nobody sees in the UI
svg.text: Three text channels steer the AI. They do not have the same visibility.
“While this information is used by AI models rather than displayed in the UI, it enables catalog-grade
metadata at scale.”
Dataset-level enrichment: size and who can see it
Dataset Description 5,000 chars visible to all consumers in the UI
Custom Instructions 5,000 chars “specifically consumed by AI agents”
File Upload 50,000 chars used by models, NOT displayed in the UI
Ten times the size of either visible field, and no reviewer meets it in the interface.
And the warning on the fields that are visible
“Do not add sensitive information to the Dataset Description or Custom Instructions fields. This
information is visible to all dataset viewers.”
COLUMN-LEVEL LIMITS
Column Description 500 chars
Additional Notes 2,000 chars
Folders grouping only
Notes carry data-quality caveats for the model.
WHAT STILL HOLDS
“All responses respect Row-Level Security
(RLS) and Column-Level Security (CLS) rules”
Enrichment steers the question, not the
rows the asker is entitled to.
Access widens by itself on 1 June 2026
Professional subscribers gain Dataset View if they are in a group a dataset was shared with, or a
folder containing shared datasets — “No action is required from authors or admins”.
View and Q&A only: no analyses, no dataset edits, no schema changes.
Legacy datasets open in the new experience carrying over data sources, joins, transformations and calculated fields.
The stack arrived in October 2025: Append, Aggregate and Pivot, faster ingestion, and up to 20 times higher
cross-source join limits than the legacy experience.
Without enrichment the agent has only column names and data types — “which are often ambiguous”.
